name: Tahath
overview: The name Tahath appears in Scripture with multiple distinct references: it is identified as a camping place for the Israelites during their wilderness journey, as seen when they encamped at Tahath and later departed from it (Numbers 33:26-27). Tahath is also the name of a Kohathite, an ancestor in the Levitical genealogy (1 Chronicles 6:24, 6:37), emphasizing his role within the priestly lineage. Additionally, Tahath is recorded as the name of two Ephraimite descendants, highlighting its use as a personal name within the tribe of Ephraim (1 Chronicles 7:20). These references collectively show Tahath as both a geographical location and a personal name significant within Israel’s tribal and Levitical history.
